before.text:
CRITICAL ZEROS OF THE RIEMANN ZETA-FUNCTION                                   3

Remark 2.1. We can apply Levinson’s method (see, for example, Appendix A of [5]) to our
choice of ψ = ψ1 + ψ2 + ψ3 . It is important to note that when applying Littlewood’s lemma,
we need to estimate the integral on the right side of a Prectangle. Assume that ψ1 (s) + ψ3 (s)
can be expressed as a Dirichlet series, ψ1 (s) + ψ3 (s) = n a(n)n−s , that integral is negligible
given that a(1) = 1. That is why we require P1 (1) + P3 (1) = 1.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Adding a mollifier shape helps only when every diagonal and cross term is controlled at compatible lengths; unjustified component lengths can create spurious proportion gains.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The reported improvement remains conditional because the required first-third twisted moment is not proved in the note.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Mollifier gains are constrained by the weakest mixed-moment interface

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The mathematical work is a controlled passage from a tractable smoothed mean square to the unsmoothed quantity needed by Littlewood's inequality. Once the seven component moments are compressed into one constant, choosing the mollifier polynomials becomes a finite optimization problem.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: A compactly supported smooth weight with derivative bounds is introduced, and Theorem 2.1 evaluates the weighted integral of |Vψ|² as a constant c times the total weight, with an error of order T times a negative power of log T. The source states that standard unsmoothing gives the corresponding integral on [1,T], then substitutes c into a lower bound for the critical-line zero proportion and reports separate polynomial choices yielding κ>0.410918 and κ*>0.40589.
directed.conceptual_reading: Smoothing is an auxiliary representation that makes the mean-value calculation stable without changing the leading objective. The proof pipeline separates analytic estimation from numerical design: all complicated moment interactions are summarized by c, and the final search varies Q and the three mollifier polynomials to reduce the logarithmic penalty.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge object is c(P1,P2,P3,Q,R,ϑ1,ϑ2,ϑ3)=c1+c2+c3+2c12+2c23+2c31. It connects seven smoothed diagonal/cross moments to an unsmoothed L² norm and then to a zero-proportion bound.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The displayed optimized coefficients are numerical witnesses, not a proof of global optimality. The deduction depends on the admissible mollifier lengths and on an unsmoothing error small enough not to alter the main term; the unit does not prove the component formulas for c.
directed.uncertainty: The pipeline and reported proportions are explicit, but the extracted polynomial coefficients, exponents, and some notation are formula-sensitive and should be checked against the scan before exact reuse.

supported: The span states the smoothing hypotheses, Theorem 2.1, the unsmoothed main term, the resulting kappa bound, and two numerical polynomial witnesses.
The warning that the coefficients are numerical witnesses rather than a global optimality certificate is appropriate.
inference: Calling smoothing an auxiliary representation and viewing the polynomial choice as a finite optimization are reasonable interpretations of the displayed pipeline.
unsupported_or_imported: Both readings count seven component moments, but c=c1+c2+c3+2c12+2c23+2c31 contains three diagonal and three cross components, not seven.
The frozen span does not name Littlewood's inequality, even though it displays the resulting kappa inequality; that attribution is imported from surrounding theory.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: The analytic-estimation-versus-numerical-design language is useful synthesis, but should not conceal the concrete six-component count.
context_or_ocr_risk: Exact exponents and polynomial coefficients remain scan-sensitive as the output says.
missed_mechanism: The output should explicitly preserve the separate admissibility bounds theta1<4/7, theta2<1/2, and theta3<1/4 when describing the optimization domain.
